newsitem.title: USA: King County, Wash., delays stadium bond vote.
newsitem.headline: King County, Wash., delays stadium bond vote.

text.p: The King County, Wash., council on Monday put off voting on a plan to sell $336 million of bonds to fund construction of a new baseball stadium for the Seattle Mariners, a spokesman said.

Citing the upward spike in interest rates and expectations of a possible move by the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, King County Executive Ron Sims had asked the county council to delay the scheduled vote on the bonds for the baseball park.
"The bond market is just too volatile," Sims said in a statement.

Jim Hattori, a finance adviser to the county, warned that rising interest rates would add to the overall cost of borrowing, and advised Sims and the council to delay the bond sale until interest rates stabilized and came down.
Stephen Kipp, a spokesman for the county, said the council hoped to vote on the bond issue next week.
"The hope is we'd vote next week," he said. "But it depends on how interest rates go."
